items.q: Which diuretic class increases urinary calcium excretion (useful pearl: causes hypocalcaemia tendency)?
items.exp: Loop blockade abolishes the electrical gradient driving paracellular calcium reabsorption, wasting calcium, while thiazides do the opposite and retain calcium. Hence loops treat hypercalcaemia after fluids; thiazides worsen it.
r: Incorrect. Thiazides retain calcium.
Correct. Loops waste urinary calcium.
Incorrect. Aldosterone blockade is calcium neutral.
Incorrect. Amiloride is also calcium neutral.
items.kp: Loops lose calcium; thiazides keep it.

items.q: Thiazides help recurrent kidney stones of which composition?
o: Calcium stones by reducing urinary calcium
items.exp: By enhancing proximal and distal calcium reabsorption, thiazides lower urinary calcium and prevent recurrent calcium stone formation in hypercalciuric patients.
r: Incorrect. Urate stones need alkalinisation and allopurinol logic.
Correct. Less urinary calcium, fewer calcium stones.
Incorrect. Cystine needs fluids and alkalinisation mainly.
Incorrect. Struvite needs infection eradication and surgery.
items.kp: Calcium stones plus high urine calcium: thiazide.

items.q: Spironolactone reduces mortality in severe heart failure mainly because it blocks what beyond diuresis?
o: Aldosterone driven cardiac fibrosis and remodelling
items.exp: Mineralocorticoid blockade prevents aldosterone mediated myocardial and vascular fibrosis, potassium and magnesium loss and sympathetic activation, yielding mortality benefit at low doses in RALES type populations.
r: Incorrect. Beta blockade is a separate pillar therapy.
Correct. Anti fibrotic aldosterone blockade saves lives.
Incorrect. Channel blockade is verapamil territory.
Incorrect. ACE inhibition is another separate pillar.
items.kp: Spironolactone in heart failure is anti fibrotic, not just diuretic.

items.q: Painful gynaecomastia on spironolactone can be reduced by switching to which agent?
items.exp: Eplerenone selectively blocks mineralocorticoid receptors without spironolactone's antiandrogen and progestogenic activity, sparing breast and menstrual side effects while retaining cardiac benefit.
r: Incorrect. Loop diuretics lack aldosterone outcome benefit.
Correct. Eplerenone is the selective switch.
Incorrect. Thiazides do not replace aldosterone blockade.
Incorrect. Mannitol is an osmotic acute agent.
items.kp: Spironolactone breast pain: switch to eplerenone.

items.q: Polyuria with dilute urine that concentrates after desmopressin indicates which diagnosis?
items.exp: Central disease lacks vasopressin secretion, so exogenous desmopressin restores aquaporin insertion and concentrates urine. Nephrogenic kidneys cannot respond to either hormone or drug.
r: Incorrect. Nephrogenic disease ignores desmopressin.
Correct. Response proves missing hormone, working kidney.
Incorrect. Polydipsia suppresses appropriately with deprivation.
Incorrect. Ketoacidosis causes osmotic, not water, diuresis.
items.kp: Desmopressin works: the hormone was missing centrally.

items.q: Lithium induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus may paradoxically improve with which diuretic?
items.exp: Mild volume contraction from thiazides increases proximal water reabsorption, reducing distal delivery and urine volume despite blocked collecting duct response, with amiloride also limiting lithium entry.
r: Incorrect. Loops worsen volume and lithium handling here.
Correct. Thiazides paradoxically cut urine volume.
Incorrect. Osmotic agents increase urine output further.
Incorrect. Spironolactone lacks this paradoxical role.
items.kp: Paradox pearl: thiazides treat nephrogenic DI.

items.q: Rapid high dose intravenous furosemide most characteristically risks which sensory toxicity?
items.exp: Loop diuretics injure cochlear stria vascularis at high peaks, especially with aminoglycosides or kidney failure, causing tinnitus and potentially permanent hearing loss, so infusion rates are capped.
r: Incorrect. Retinal toxicity belongs to other drug classes.
Correct. Cochlear injury is the loop warning.
Incorrect. Optic neuritis is ethambutol's signature.
Incorrect. Smell loss is not diuretic pharmacology.
items.kp: Fast furosemide pushes can deafen; infuse slowly.

items.q: Mannitol's main therapeutic niches are which pair?
o: Raised intracranial pressure and acute glaucoma crises
items.exp: Osmotic mannitol draws brain and eye water intravascularly for acute pressure emergencies, while its diuresis is a side effect unsuited to chronic volume therapy and dangerous in heart failure.
r: Incorrect. Chronic pressure uses tubule blocking diuretics.
Correct. Brain and eye pressure emergencies.
Incorrect. Mannitol can precipitate pulmonary oedema in failure.
Incorrect. It increases, not decreases, urine water loss.
items.kp: Mannitol pulls water from brain and eye, not chronic ankles.

items.q: The most dangerous electrolyte consequence of combining spironolactone with ACE inhibitor in kidney impairment is what?
items.exp: Dual suppression of aldosterone signalling plus reduced filtration retains potassium to arrhythmogenic levels, mandating baseline and follow up potassium and creatinine checks after initiation or dose change.
r: Incorrect. Both drugs retain, not waste, potassium.
Correct. Potassium climbs dangerously.
Incorrect. Sodium effects are secondary here.
Incorrect. Calcium is not the pairing danger.
items.kp: Two potassium retainers plus weak kidneys: check potassium.

items.q: Acetazolamide relieves acute mountain sickness mainly by causing what acid base effect?
items.exp: Carbonic anhydrase blockade wastes bicarbonate, and the resulting metabolic acidosis drives compensatory hyperventilation that mimics acclimatisation, while also lowering eye and cerebrospinal fluid production.
r: Incorrect. Ventilation compensates; primary effect is metabolic.
Correct. Bicarbonate loss acidifies and stimulates breathing.
Incorrect. Potassium shifts are minor beside the acid effect.
Incorrect. It diureses rather than retains water.
items.kp: Acetazolamide acidifies blood to speed altitude acclimatisation.
